slides.title: Can profit rise while cash stays tight?
options: Profit and cash must move together
Profit and cash can move differently
slides.prompt: Before the example, explain what each number measures.

notes.say: Ask for a reason, not just a vote. Profit records performance under accrual accounting. Cash records actual movements. We will reconcile them with a simplified example.

slides.title: Receivables absorb part of the reported profit
slides.exhibit: Simplified operating cash reconciliation · INR lakh

chart.alt: Profit plus depreciation less the increase in receivables gives operating cash in this simplified example.

notes.say: Assume no other noncash adjustments, working-capital movements or operating cash items. Depreciation reduced accounting profit but was not a cash payment this period. The receivables increase represents sales not collected in cash.

slides.title: What happens if customers pay sooner?
options: Operating cash increases, all else equal
Profit must increase by the same amount
slides.prompt: Explain the timing effect before checking the answer in notes.

notes.say: With the same recognised sales and all other inputs unchanged, faster collection reduces the receivables increase and raises operating cash. It need not change recognised profit. Keep this explanation available in a circulated handout.
